dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats every 13.2 days but alternating dips differ in depth and a strong second dip appears about a quarter of an orbit later, ~26% as deep as the main dip. Transit depths also scatter between sectors and between individual events far more than a planet should. Together this is best explained by a close eclipsing binary star on the target, folded at its primary eclipse, rather than a 3.3 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Significant second dip at phase 0.279, ~26% the primary depth, offset ~0.221 from half-phase, indicates stellar companion (eccentric eclipsing binary) with significant secondary occultation, not planetary.
Odd and even eclipses differ at >3 sigma (ratio ~1.5), consistent with eccentric EB folded at primary period rather than single planet.
Four transits are not consistent; formal per-transit depth scatter is highly significant, arguing against several identical planetary transits.
Sector depths change >50% (1566 ppm in sector 42 vs 2776 ppm in sector 70 vs 2587 ppm in sector 92) with 3 sectors only.

Tool confirms apparent sector change is not a calibration difference between light-curve products; depths truly differ sector to sector for this signal while SPOC 2-min and TESS-SPOC each have one sector.
